title: Complex Homographs with Phonological Alternation
objectives: Identify homographs with different pronunciations based on meaning
Master vowel and voicing shifts in homograph pairs
Retrieve correct homograph pronunciation rapidly from context

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner reads "read" as /riːd/ in past tense context.
💡 Solution: Check verb tense before reading aloud: Yesterday I /rɛd/.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Complex Homographs with Phonological Alternation
1. Definition: Homographs are words written identically that have different pronunciations and meanings.

2. Rule: 1. bow: /boʊ/ (ribbon/weapon) vs /baʊ/ (bend/ship front). 2. tear: /tɪər/ (crying) vs /tɛər/ (rip). 3. wind: /wɪnd/ (air) vs /waɪnd/ (twist). 4. lead: /liːd/ (guide) vs /lɛd/ (metal). 5. read: /riːd/ (present) vs /rɛd/ (past). 6. close: /kloʊz/ (verb) vs /kloʊs/ (adjective). 7. house: /haʊz/ (verb) vs /haʊs/ (noun).
3. Why? Unrelated words or historical sound shifts merged into identical spellings.
4. How to recognize? Analyze syntax and sentence context to determine meaning.
5. Common examples: a ribbon bow /boʊ/ vs to bow /baʊ/ down; a tear /tɪər/ in eye vs to tear /tɛər/ paper; strong wind /wɪnd/ vs wind /waɪnd/ a clock; lead /liːd/ team vs lead /lɛd/ pipe
6. Counter-examples: Homophones (different spelling, same sound: see/sea).
7. Exceptions: Regional dialectal variation in homograph pairs.
8. Common mistakes: Reading "I read a book yesterday" as /riːd/ instead of past /rɛd/.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Read the sentence FIRST to know the meaning, THEN pronounce the homograph!
10. Key vocabulary: homograph, phonological alternation, context decoding, voicing shift, syntactic category
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🟣 C1
13. Associated Visual: 🎭 Two masks on a single word showing double pronunciation.
14. Key Takeaway: Context determines homograph sound! Lead /liːd/ (guide) vs Lead /lɛd/ (metal)!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: How do you pronounce "lead" in "lead the team" vs "heavy lead pipe"? (guide = /liːd/; metal = /lɛd/)
CCQ 2: How do you pronounce "tear" in "tears in eyes" vs "tear paper"? (crying = /tɪər/; rip = /tɛər/)
CCQ 3: How does "close" change between verb "close the door" and adjective "close friend"? (verb = /kloʊz/ with z; adjective = /kloʊs/ with s)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Select correct pronunciation for the homograph in context:
🎯 Item: Please close /kloʊz/ the door. ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Verb = /kloʊz/ (with Z)
🎯 Item: He is a close /kloʊs/ friend. ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Adjective = /kloʊs/ (with S)
🎯 Item: The wind /wɪnd/ is blowing. ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Air = /wɪnd/
